tasks.desc: Validate the pairwise incompatibility rule with a brute-force harness.
Implement the actual solver: normalize intervals, compute prev via endpoint arrays and two monotonic segment-tree modes per direction, build prefix max, and answer queries.
Verify the solver on the provided samples (passed) and edge cases covered by the prior brute-force validation.
Optimize for the constraints: process one mode at a time, use packed ints/bisect, fast I/O, and free structures between passes.
Finalize the solution; no failing samples or counterexamples remain.

proposals: First validate the pairwise incompatibility rule on small random instances with a brute-force constraint solver using equality contraction and topological ordering or cycle detection.

Try the supplied latest-previous method: endpoint arrays plus two strict crossing rectangles in a 2D range-max update / point-query structure per direction, then prefix maximum over latest-bad indices for O(1) queries.
Try the dual reverse-sweep method: endpoint minimum arrays plus a 2D point-update / range-min structure per direction to compute earliest-future bad indices, then suffix minimum for O(1) queries.
If max-based 2D structures are too heavy, try the sliding-window method with 2D BIT range counting and two-pointer over L/R, maintaining conflict counts under add/remove.
Keep offline parallel binary search with 3D dominance, or a carefully designed block/sqrt decomposition, as fallbacks, but expect them to be more complex or slower in Python.
prev: Replace the validation harness with the actual solver: read the real input, normalize each person to (l,r,dir), compute prev[i] for all incompatible earlier pairs using (a) opposite-direction same l/r last-index arrays, (b) same-direction same l/r last-index arrays, and (c) two online monotonic segment trees per direction for crossing same-direction intervals (mode A: range-update interior [l+1,r-1] with key=r, point-query at l with threshold r; mode B: range-update interior with key=N-l, point-query at r with threshold N-l-1), then build prefix max bad and answer each query [L,R] with Yes iff bad[R] < L; test on samples and random small cases against the brute-force oracle.
